canonical_posts.title: The receipt convention keeps the work honest
canonical_posts.subtitle: Every consequential agent action writes a short note. A daily job reads the notes. A one-page summary goes to Telegram with coffee. Here is why that system exists.

canonical_posts.title: How I moved one idea through every surface I own
canonical_posts.subtitle: A conceptual shift cascaded through the philosophy page, landing copy, pillar cards, animations, and resume in a single week. This is about how consistency works when one person owns everything.

canonical_posts.title: What 14 principles taught me about operating as one person
canonical_posts.subtitle: I had 14 founder principles. I cut them to 9. Here is what the compression taught me about distilling your own operating system.

canonical_posts.title: A release nobody is allowed to cut is not a release
canonical_posts.subtitle: Three fail-closed gates landed in one week. The one that stalled the work was the gate I had reserved for myself.

canonical_posts.title: The quality bar I ratified failed first on my own page
canonical_posts.subtitle: I ratified a quality bar on a Tuesday. The first thing it caught was an inflated claim on my own founder page.

canonical_posts.title: I took myself out of the approval path for a system that writes its own tools
canonical_posts.subtitle: On 2026-08-01 I removed the per-skill human gate from the autonomous learning loop and replaced it with policy, receipts, automatic demotion and a kill file.

canonical_posts.title: The most useful thing I shipped that week was an accurate description of work already done
canonical_posts.subtitle: A thin week on the fleet. One closing pass on the game, and a roadmap that had been wrong for seventeen days getting corrected.

canonical_posts.title: Nine projects were carrying real work that had never left this machine
canonical_posts.subtitle: On one day I committed local working state in nine repositories. Until that morning, losing the laptop meant losing all of it.

canonical_posts.title: There was a daemon running on my main machine that nothing documented
canonical_posts.subtitle: I wrote a runbook for a process that had been running on my primary workstation with no owner, no documentation and no way for anyone else to touch it.

canonical_posts.title: An outside audit cut my animation timings in half and it was right
canonical_posts.subtitle: A motion audit from someone who does this for a living took my banner animation from 1.8 seconds to 0.8 and changed two repositories in a day.

canonical_posts.title: The first thing my marketing agent produced is not allowed to send itself
canonical_posts.subtitle: A four touch outbound sequence, written by an agent, landed marked draft only with four named blockers standing between it and a single email.
